body.heading: Comfort is a strategy, not an indulgence
paragraphs: There are days when the goal is not growth, productivity or insight. The goal is simply to get through the day with your kindness towards yourself intact. On those days, small comforts are not a distraction from the work. They are the work.
The trick is to choose them in advance. A hard day is the worst possible time to brainstorm what might help, because hard days are exactly when the mind insists nothing will.

body.heading: Make your list on an ordinary day
paragraphs: Write down five to ten small things that reliably soften a day for you: a particular walk, a hot drink made slowly, a shower, a favourite song played loudly, twenty minutes with a comforting book, texting one specific person, sitting in the sunniest spot in the house.

Keep the list somewhere findable — the front of a notebook, a note on your phone. Include at least a couple that cost nothing and can be done at home, for the days when even leaving the house is too much.

body.heading: Know when a hard day needs more than comfort
paragraphs: Small comforts are for hard days, and they are good at their job. But if low mood, anxiety or exhaustion settles in for weeks, starts shrinking your life, or ever feels unsafe, that is beyond the reach of comfort lists — and beyond the reach of this article.

Please treat that as a sign to bring in people: a trusted adult, a doctor, a counsellor or a helpline in your country. Resilience includes knowing when the load should be shared with professionals, and sharing it early is a strong move, not a last resort.

takeaway: List your small comforts while life is calm, so a hard day never has to improvise.
